title: Resurrection of the Body
english: …Admiring its beauty, the body is sown in corruption, weakness, and dishonor, but it will be raised in honor, incorruption, and power, even though it has been dejected. The prophet's wisdom is worthy of admiration; by comparing the nature of the matter to a seed, he skillfully and most wisely provides a parable for the body's corruption.

The body will be raised not naked, but rather well-clothed in incorruption, glory, and strength; and moreover, this will be enhanced by the spiritual mindset, through a certain transformation by the grace from above and the incomparable power of the All-Creator toward all that is in Him. For in the fallen body, which is sown as if into the earth, there resides corruption, weakness, ugliness, and a psychic mindset, which we say is the same as the fleshly and earthly one; for it was present at the beginning in its natural state, but entered through transgression and the judgment of death, our nature crying out to its original state.

The restoration of what was lost is being worked out by the necessity of God's power and energy, and we are being renewed in the participation of the good things that were present in the beginning; for we are being renewed in Christ according to the scriptures. For a holy prophet says, 'Take courage, Zion, do not let your hands be weak; the Lord your God is in you, powerful to save you and to renew you in his love' (Isaiah 40:9-10). For when God and Father loved us, He then renewed us in Christ; and it is true that everything in Him is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17); and the old things have passed away, and new things have come (Revelation 21:5).

What are the old things? The things that have passed away; and what are the new things? The things that have been selected. The old is corruption, and indeed the perishable, and moreover the difficult, and the vices of the psychic mindset; but through Christ, the new things are glory, incorruption, power, and the spiritual mindset, for our body shall be spiritual. What, then, would the spiritual be, if I were to be a mystagogue? Will it no longer be flesh, and will it not be composed at all, just as it is now composed of bones and nerves? No; for if some think that the body falling to the ground will be something like this—weak and airy and yielding only a few shadows—they are wrong. It will not be resurrected as something merely similar to the first, but something else entirely. I would say that the spiritual body is not a shadow in the form of an incorporeal spirit, but rather a body that has been separated from the fleshly and earthly mindset.
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence with 'κάλλους ἀναφὺς θαυμάζεται' (Admiring its beauty...)
The translation of 'ἀναφὺς' is contextually interpreted as 'admiring its beauty' or 'through its beauty'.
The word 'κατημφιασμένον' (dejected/brought low) was added to the first paragraph.
baehrens: PG 74; Fragmenta in 1 Cor u07 rem early

title: Psychic and Spiritual
english: If someone were to describe the body from our earth as psychic, they would reasonably not attribute the form of the soul to it.
Instead, they would turn the power of the word to the psychic or carnal mindset, just as we also consider wisdom to be psychic and earthly, related to human nature.
For example, it is said that marriage and the bed are honorable and undefiled (Hebrews 13:4).
This is because a driving motion has been implanted in the nature of the body by the creator of all things, stirring the animal to procreate.
As it has been said to man, 'Increase and multiply and fill the earth' (Genesis 1:28), and the one who formed, says, in the beginning, 'male and female he made them' (Genesis 1:27).
Therefore, the inclination towards childbearing alone is without blame.
However, as far as it pertains to the nature of the one acting, the passion would be either carnal or psychic.
It is written that the psychic man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him (1 Corinthians 2:14).
The spiritual man, on the other hand, examines all things, but is not examined by anyone.
Since it was necessary to confirm the word with deeds, it says that the first man Adam became a living soul, and the last Adam became a life-giving spirit (1 Corinthians 15:45).
Therefore, Adam was named psychic, for this is what it means to be made into a living soul, not completely free from carnal desires.

The desires and passions that are inclined towards the things of the flesh, even if they have a law as an advocate, would still be considered weaknesses of the flesh according to the truth, if one looks at the nature of the things done.
The first man Adam was given a living soul, but the second man, Christ, who is from heaven, came not into a soul but into a spirit that gives life.
For the Word of God, who is by nature God, united the human to himself, and lived a life that is divine and fitting for God and completely blameless.
He did not commit sin, having a mind untouched by external pleasures and not overcome by desires for food.
For even if he is seen to have partaken of food and drink, it was to show that he was truly human like us, but he made the drinking free.
For he was in the flesh for our sake, but beyond the flesh; for he was a life-giving spirit as God.

But the first man Adam did not receive the desire for food without blame; for he was made into a living soul and, overcome by the pleasure of food, he ate from the tree of life, although the divine law forbade it.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the end.
The translation of 'ψυχικόν' as 'psychic' is not exact, but it is the closest equivalent in English.
The phrase 'ἐπίγειον τὴν καθ' ἡμᾶς' is translated as 'related to human nature' to convey the idea of something being related to the physical world.
baehrens: PG 74; Fragmenta in 1 Cor u07 rem mid

title: First and Second Adam
english: The distinction between the first and second Adam is not a matter of different natures, but rather a difference in the quality of their lives, characters, and ways of living.
The first Adam was earthly and carnal in his mindset, while the second Adam is spiritual and from heaven.
The quality of their mindset and the way they chose to live differed, one being psychic, the other spiritual.
The spiritual did not come first, but the psychic, and then the spiritual.
The psychic body is sown into the earth, and it is not unacceptable to human nature to transition from a psychic mindset to a spiritual one.
The psychic is older than the spiritual.
What would be the faith of such people?
The first human, Adam, was created from the earth and was earthly and carnal.
The second, who is full, is from heaven.
For even if the Word of God became flesh according to the scriptures, and the one from heaven is above all.
Thus, both stood in earthly bodies, but not in equal ways of life or mindset.

As we have borne the image of the earthly, that is, the likeness to Adam, and have been overcome by passions and weaknesses that lead to sin, although we have been sold under the yoke of corruption, so we will bear the image of the heavenly, that is, Christ.
Having become superior to fleshly desires and the will to sin, and having already conquered the formerly powerful and invincible death that tyrannized us.
For flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God.
The mystery of the resurrection is established through this transformation.
For as long as the human body is flesh and blood, that is, mortal and corruptible, it cannot inherit the kingdom of God.
Therefore, it is necessary for corruption to be swallowed up and for the mortal to be transformed into immortality, and for it to be glorified with a certain divine and ineffable glory.
For then it will inherit the kingdom of God.
Behold, I tell you a mystery: not all will sleep, but all will be changed.
translator_notes: The Greek text contains the phrase 'ὁ γεμὴν 315 δεύτερος' which appears to be a fragment or corruption; the number 315 is not translatable and may be a scribal artifact.

The Greek text ends abruptly with 'αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστι καὶ τῶν ἔσεσθαι προσδοκωμένων' and does not complete the thought; the trailing words are rendered literally with ellipsis to reflect the edge fragment.
baehrens: PG 74; Fragmenta in 1 Cor u07 rem close
